In the beginning, when we started, you were judged by your ability to copy records. I was very good at it. He wasn't. So my band was probably bigger than his, locally. But I recognised something in him that was unique. Because he couldn't copy so well, it turned out to be a good thing – it turned into his writing style. He wasn't ever going to be an impersonator. He was just too original.

I was the first one to encourage him to put out a solo record. I recognised Nebraska, immediately. The minute he played it for me – I was the first one he played it for. He thought he was making demos for Born in the USA. But I was like 'That's the most remarkable record I've ever heard.' I said 'Yeah. And it's gonna be the most intimate record you ever make in your life, because you had no intention of releasing it.' Every singer is an actor, whether they realise it or not. That thing was like an acting job beyond anything he'd ever done. He really became those characters.
